Find or identify birds mainly by their calls and other field sounds, listening to the surrounding environment. Recordings or audio recognition at home are different from observing birds in the field.

entries.localizedLabel: Observe the stars or practice astronomy
entries.localizedDescription: Observe celestial objects and phenomena in the day or night sky with the unaided eye or an instrument. Reading about astronomy or working with data indoors is a different mode.

entries.localizedLabel: Explore unusual or abandoned urban sites (urbex)
entries.localizedDescription: Explore unusual or abandoned urban architecture and infrastructure from outside or with authorized access, observing and documenting it. Dangerous or unauthorized entry is not implied.
Examine a plant and identify its species or family from observable features or a key. Collecting the plant is not implied.

entries.localizedLabel: Do a scavenger hunt or clue-based quest
entries.localizedDescription: Search for a list of real objects or clues and confirm what you find. This is broader than the specific rules of geocaching or letterboxing.

entries.localizedLabel: Draw or photograph outdoors on site
entries.localizedDescription: Draw or photograph on location while directly observing a subject or landscape in the field. The method may be drawing or using a camera; a trip or walk may be an additional meaning.

entries.localizedLabel: Search for minerals, rocks, and fossils
entries.localizedDescription: Search for and examine geological specimens or fossils, and collect them when permitted, as a collecting activity. Industrial extraction and collecting in protected areas are not implied.
localizedAliases: Search for minerals, rocks, and fossils

entries.localizedDescription: Gather wild berries or plants for personal use in a place where it is permitted. Identifying species or taking a walk may accompany the gathering but is not synonymous with it.
At low tide, examine pools in the intertidal zone and observe their organisms and surroundings. Collecting organisms is not required.
Travel on a multi-day walking route with a carried backpack and overnight stops along the way. This integrated trekking format differs from car camping at a base.
Spend the night in a minimal, temporary camp directly along a route or in the open. It is a simple, short-term stop rather than an equipped campground.
Stay in a tent or with camping gear beside a car or at a campsite, bringing the gear by vehicle. Backpacking on foot is not implied.

entries.localizedLabel: Take a caravan or camping holiday
entries.localizedDescription: Spend a holiday with overnight stays in a caravan, camper, or at campsites, moving between pitches. The lodging format does not mean driving for the entire period.
Stay outdoors in pre-equipped, comfortable accommodation such as a tent or cabin. This is a lodging style, not a walking trek or pitching your own tent.

entries.localizedLabel: Stay in a motorhome or RV
entries.localizedDescription: Travel or stay overnight in a motorhome or RV and use its living facilities. Driving and resting at a campsite are distinct activities.
Pitch a tent and spend time outdoors, including overnight. Camping is a lodging or trip format; hiking, cooking, and sleeping may be separate segments.

entries.localizedLabel: Ride an inflatable tube for fun
entries.localizedDescription: Ride an inflatable tube for play or recreation, sliding down a snowy slope or floating on water, such as a river or a towed water tube. The setting and propulsion vary; this is not limited to snow tubing.
localizedAliases: Ride an inflatable tube for fun

entries.localizedDescription: Ride in a pleasure boat as a passenger or operate one for recreational boating. Rowing, sailing, and motor navigation are different ways to take part.

entries.localizedLabel: Take a leisure outing by kayak or SUP
entries.localizedDescription: Paddle a kayak or canoe, or stand on a SUP board, for a relaxed outing on the water. Kayaking and SUP use different equipment and postures; racing, surfing, and workout sessions are different modes.

entries.localizedLabel: Hunt or shoot outdoors for recreation (personal choice)
entries.localizedDescription: Take part in recreational hunting or shooting in a natural setting as permitted by local rules; searching, stalking, and shooting are distinct methods. This is not wildlife observation, and the activity is not presumed harmless or unlawful.
Operate a sailboat or yacht, or take part in a recreational outing under sail, using the wind for propulsion. An official race or regatta is a different competitive context.
Launch, hold, and steer a kite in an open area. A picnic may be a concurrent setting; making the kite is a separate maker project.

entries.localizedLabel: Go for a relaxed horseback ride
entries.localizedDescription: Ride a horse at a relaxed pace along a chosen route and enjoy the outing. A riding lesson, working with the horse, or a competition may be separate contexts.
Cast or lower fishing gear, watch for a bite, and bring in fish as part of recreational fishing. The type of fishing, catch-and-release, or keeping a catch can be specified as context or a variant.

Swim near the surface with a mask and snorkel while observing underwater life. Brief dives may occur, but scuba with a tank and athletic apnea or freediving involve different breathing methods or exertion.

Climb a protected rock route using a continuous steel safety cable, carabiners, and steps for progress. It is a protected hiking route rather than an ordinary rock-climbing route, but requires specialized equipment and skills.

entries.localizedLabel: Do acoustic birding or count night migrants
entries.localizedDescription: Listen for and identify birds by their calls or songs in the field (acoustic birding). This can also include the narrower, separate practice of recording or counting nocturnal flight calls from migrating birds; acoustic birding as a whole is not limited to night migration.
Repeatedly measure or record selected geological or ecological indicators at a site to track changes over time. A one-off visit without a series of observations is not necessarily monitoring.

entries.localizedLabel: Run or take part in a BioBlitz
entries.localizedDescription: Organize or join a time-limited, intensive BioBlitz: observe and record as many species as possible at a chosen site. This is an event or project, not a single identification technique.
Record observed bird species in an ongoing list or checklist, noting place and date and optionally the number of individuals. Searching for birds is a preceding or concurrent activity.

entries.localizedLabel: Record weather observations for a project
entries.localizedDescription: Regularly observe and enter weather measurements for a citizen-science project using its protocol. Simply noticing rain or checking a forecast is not project monitoring.

entries.localizedLabel: Record an observation, with species, media, or conditions
entries.localizedDescription: Document a field finding: species or trait, place and time, and, when needed, a photo, audio, or description of conditions. Recording it is not the same as later verifying the identification.

entries.localizedLabel: Add or check a taxonomic label
entries.localizedDescription: Add or check the taxonomic label (organism name or group) on an observation using available features or identification keys. A comment or confirming the record may be separate steps.
Review a photo or record already uploaded by another participant and suggest a species or taxonomic identification. This is online community validation, not your own field encounter.

entries.localizedLabel: Label images or audio for a citizen-science project
entries.localizedDescription: Annotate images or audio recordings according to a project protocol by marking objects, features, sounds, or time intervals. This does not involve collecting new recordings in the field.
localizedAliases: Label audio data for a citizen-science project

entries.localizedLabel: Check an observation’s quality, location, or date
entries.localizedDescription: Review a user-submitted field record for completeness and plausible coordinates, date, and metadata without replacing its taxonomic identification.

entries.localizedLabel: Transcribe a historical document or archive record
entries.localizedDescription: Transfer a handwritten or scanned historical source into editable text, preserving the words that can be read and marking illegible passages. This is crowdsourced archival work, not passive reading.
Practice a chosen meditation or mindfulness technique. A particular goal or tradition is optional; simply resting without doing anything can be recorded differently.
Spend time in quiet rest without an intentional external task. Sleep and screen-based content are separate chosen activities.

entries.localizedLabel: Reflect, observe your thoughts, daydream, or contemplate
entries.localizedDescription: Think things over, consider a question, daydream, or observe your thoughts and surroundings. This may be deliberate or free-form. Formal meditation is a possible separate personal practice, not a required distinction.

entries.localizedLabel: Browse shop windows without planning a purchase
entries.localizedDescription: Take your time looking at shops or their windows without a specific purchase in mind. Purposeful shopping or completing a purchase can be recorded separately.
localizedAliases: Browse shops without planning a purchase

entries.localizedLabel: Deliver orders and freight as work
entries.localizedDescription: Transport orders, materials, mail, or goods as part of a job.
localizedAliases: Deliver orders, materials, mail, or goods as work

entries.localizedLabel: Drive or operate a vehicle professionally
entries.localizedDescription: Professionally operate a vehicle or machine; this does not mean riding as a passenger.

entries.localizedLabel: Clean or service a facility professionally
entries.localizedDescription: Professionally clean or maintain a building, site, or facility.
localizedAliases: Clean or maintain a facility for work

entries.localizedDescription: Carry out building or facility operations and related operational work.
Load or unload cargo, or move it from place to place.
Gather items for an order, assemble or kit them, and pack them.

entries.localizedLabel: Receive, check, and put away stock
entries.localizedDescription: Accept a delivery or goods, check them against the shipment, and put them in their assigned place.

entries.localizedLabel: Route and dispatch orders or vehicles
entries.localizedDescription: Plan or assign routes and dispatch an order or vehicle.

entries.localizedLabel: Prepare a shipment and hand it to a carrier
entries.localizedDescription: Prepare the shipment and its paperwork, then transfer it to the carrier.
Put stock in place, replenish it, and maintain inventory.

entries.localizedLabel: Control traffic, access, or a safety zone
entries.localizedDescription: Manage movement, access, or the boundaries of a safe work zone.

entries.localizedLabel: Inspect a vehicle or machine before a shift or handoff
entries.localizedDescription: Inspect a vehicle or piece of equipment before a shift or when handing it over.

entries.localizedLabel: Service or repair a work vehicle
entries.localizedDescription: Maintain or repair a vehicle used professionally.

entries.localizedLabel: Collect, sort, or process waste and recyclables
entries.localizedDescription: Collect, sort, or process waste or recyclable materials.

entries.localizedLabel: Sort, inspect, or route returns and defective goods
entries.localizedDescription: Sort, inspect, or route returned or defective goods. Map specific repair or repacking to the matching canonical activity when tracked separately.

entries.localizedLabel: Sort, label, or assign goods by use or quality
entries.localizedDescription: Sort or label materials or goods, or assign them by intended use or quality.
localizedAliases: Sort or label goods by quality

entries.localizedLabel: Stage tools, materials, or a workspace for another worker
entries.localizedDescription: Provide or prepare tools, materials, and a work area for another person carrying out a task.

entries.localizedLabel: Monitor a ship’s power systems or equipment
entries.localizedDescription: Monitor the indicators or equipment of a vessel’s power system.
Stand watch or monitor the operation of a vessel.

entries.localizedLabel: Browse a feed or other media
entries.localizedDescription: Browse a feed, websites, or a collection of material, moving from one post or item to another.

entries.localizedLabel: Listen to audio or a podcast
entries.localizedDescription: Listen to a podcast, recording, broadcast, or other material that is primarily spoken.
Choose to listen to recorded or streamed music as an activity.
Watch a film, series, or individual episode.
Watch video clips, programs, or streams without specifying a film or series.

entries.localizedLabel: Carry out a military service duty
entries.localizedDescription: Record carrying out an assigned military, service, or operational duty at a neutral level. Service profile is recorded through `axis.role` or `axis.discipline`; use general nodes for specific observed work such as command, training, logistics, monitoring, or maintenance. The label does not reveal tactics, use-of-force methods, or restricted information.

entries.localizedLabel: Travel to a social, community, or spiritual event
entries.localizedDescription: Travel by vehicle or on foot to a social gathering, community event, or spiritual practice. Waiting along the way may be part of the route.
Travel by any means to or from work or a place of study.
Travel, walk, transport goods, or accompany someone for a household errand.
localizedAliases: Trip to a repair or service provider

entries.localizedLabel: Travel or transport for own-use production
entries.localizedDescription: Travel, walk, transport goods, or accompany people as part of own-use production.

entries.localizedLabel: Travel for personal care or a service
entries.localizedDescription: Travel or walk, and wait along the route, for personal care or a service for yourself.
Travel to a chosen destination for an errand or as part of a journey.
Wait for transport, a connection, or the next part of a journey.
Walk in order to reach a chosen place.
Exercise with the primary goal of developing endurance.
Walk a route as training or deliberate physical exertion.
Do exercises for joint mobility, flexibility, and stretching.
Train or take part in a chosen sport by practicing its movements, techniques, and game actions.
Exercise with resistance, weights, or body weight to develop strength.
Prepare and carry out 3D printing or post-process a part.

entries.localizedLabel: Assemble a product at a station or line
entries.localizedDescription: Assemble a product at a workstation or on a production line.
localizedAliases: Assemble a product at a station or line

entries.localizedDescription: Bind, fold, trim, or otherwise finish printed materials from a production run.

entries.localizedLabel: Check a product against quality standards
entries.localizedDescription: Inspect a product, its parameters, or its dimensions against a standard.
Maintain workshop tools, production tooling, or fixtures.

entries.localizedLabel: Monitor a production line and correct deviations
entries.localizedDescription: Monitor the process or its parameters and address deviations.
localizedAliases: Monitor process parameters and correct deviations

entries.localizedDescription: Operate a machine, piece of equipment, or production line to manufacture goods.
localizedAliases: Operate a production machine or line

entries.localizedDescription: Pack or label finished products.

entries.localizedLabel: Prepare equipment for a production run
entries.localizedDescription: Prepare or reconfigure a machine or workstation for a production batch.
localizedAliases: Prepare or change over a machine for a batch

entries.localizedLabel: Prepare files and forms for print production
entries.localizedDescription: Prepare text, layout, or printing plates for a print run, including prepress checks. This is separate from designing the original, running the press, or binding the finished work when tracked as separate segments.
localizedAliases: Prepare materials and plates for a print run

entries.localizedDescription: Process food raw materials into products for storage or sale. Distinguish this from preparing and serving food for immediate consumption or a guest.

entries.localizedLabel: Process materials or components for manufacturing
entries.localizedDescription: Process a material or component using a manufacturing method.
Configure digital or numerical controls for a manufacturing operation.
localizedAliases: Set up numerical controls for production

entries.localizedLabel: Record a production run, batch, or result
entries.localizedDescription: Create a production record for a run, batch, or result.
Rework an item that did not pass quality control.
localizedAliases: Rework an item that failed inspection

entries.localizedDescription: Print a production run of printed materials. This excludes creating the graphic original or preparing materials for printing when those are separate segments.
Sew garments, soft goods, or textile products. Designing clothing and repairing an existing item are related but distinct actions.
Test a product after assembly.
Produce textile fabric by interlacing or knitting yarns. The specific material can be recorded on the material axis.
Perform paired or group gymnastics balances, lifts, throws, catches, and acrobatic elements as part of a joint routine.
Perform an aerobic gymnastics routine combining aerobic movement with strength, dynamic, jumping, and flexibility elements. Individual, pair, or group composition depends on the format.

entries.localizedLabel: Shoot an air rifle at a target
entries.localizedDescription: Take part in target shooting with an air rifle in the Target Sprint discipline.
Ride a sled down a natural ice track, steering to control direction and speed. The format and track conditions vary by event.
Practice krabi krabong through martial exercises and forms using traditional Thai swords and a staff or pole.
Compete in Muay Talay by balancing and trying to knock an opponent off a narrow beam or log under the rules of the event.
Perform Wai Kru, a ritualized dance ceremony associated with Muay Thai. Taking part in a contest or demonstration of the ceremony differs from sparring.
Practice Sanda wushu in contact bouts, using permitted hand and foot strikes and throws under Sanda rules.
Take part in show skiing by performing water-ski tricks and synchronized group figures in a staged performance.
Swim using a monofin or two fins, propelling yourself by muscular effort at the surface or underwater.
Play at the bottom of a pool: use a short stick to move a puck and score in the opposing team’s goal while swimming with a mask, snorkel, and fins.
Play a contact team game underwater: hold and pass a ball and place it in a basket-shaped goal on the pool bottom, using a mask, snorkel, and fins.
Navigate underwater using a compass and distance measurements, find or pass control points, and complete a set course while remaining submerged.
Shoot at a target underwater with a speargun or harpoon while holding your breath. The event scores hits and, in some formats, speed moving between targets.
Swim and perform movement or expressive elements at the surface and underwater while wearing a mermaid tail with a monofin.
Wrestle one-on-one in and under the water, trying to remove a ribbon from the opponent’s ankle and show it above the water.
Ride a mountain bike between control points, using a map and route and choosing a path between points.
Use cross-country skis to navigate by map and pass control points along a chosen route.
In Trail-O, determine from a control station which marker corresponds to the control point shown on the map, following the event’s accuracy or timing rules.
Play field lacrosse by catching, passing, and throwing a ball with a stick on an outdoor field.
Play lacrosse Sixes, a compact, fast-paced format with six players and its own rules.
Perform choreographed individual or group kickboxing movements and techniques to music, without sparring.
Perform kata in karate: a prescribed sequence of offensive and defensive techniques in a set order and direction.
Compete in kumite by sparring with a karate opponent and scoring with permitted techniques under WKF rules.

entries.localizedLabel: Play Guts with a flying disc
entries.localizedDescription: Play Guts by throwing a disc at the opposing team, whose players try to catch it in the target zone.
Perform individual or paired trick combinations using a flying disc, with throws and catches.
Play Double Disc Court (DDC): two teams throw two discs at the other side at the same time under DDC rules.
Run a course while throwing a disc toward checkpoints or the finish in Discathon.

entries.localizedLabel: Practice accuracy or distance disc throwing
entries.localizedDescription: Practice throwing a flying disc for accuracy or distance. The specific exercise can be recorded separately.
Throw a disc, run or position yourself under its flight, and catch it while recording time or distance in MTA/TRC.
Play Goaltimate, a team flying-disc game with goals or a hoop and its own rules.
Play Discflect, a team flying-disc game with a target zone and its own rules.
Perform choreographed combinations in a disco style to the rhythm of the music, in practice or competition.
Dance merengue using its characteristic partnered or solo step pattern to merengue music.
Perform selected American Smooth ballroom dances, with characteristic travel across the floor and partner leading.
Perform selected American Rhythm ballroom dances with a partner, using their characteristic rhythms and technique.
Dance acrobatic rock and roll as a pair, performing fast rock-and-roll steps, jumps, and supported acrobatic elements.
Dance Boogie Woogie, a partnered swing dance with characteristic rhythm and steps and competitive improvisation.
Dance Bugg, a partnered swing dance with characteristic steps and figures under Bugg rules.
Play carom billiards by striking your cue ball so that it contacts both object balls, under carom rules.
Play English billiards by using a cue to strike the white and object balls and score under English billiards rules.

entries.localizedLabel: Compete in a rally car race
entries.localizedDescription: Compete in an automobile rally by completing timed special stages and the connecting routes under rally rules.

entries.localizedLabel: Compete in an off-road car race or rally raid
entries.localizedDescription: Compete in an off-road automobile race or rally raid, driving a challenging navigation course or special stages under FIA competition rules.
Pilot an unpowered aircraft and use rising air currents to gain altitude and travel along a route.

entries.localizedLabel: Perform aerobatics in an airplane or glider
entries.localizedDescription: Perform aerobatic maneuvers in an airplane or glider, completing a sequence of figures in a defined airspace.

Take part in the aeromodelling family of activities. Building a model and operating it in flight are distinct activities and may be timed separately, or the user may record the full aeromodelling session.
A flight-family option covering two distinct piloted aircraft modes. Record the whole selected flight session or refine it to one of the two modes.

entries.localizedLabel: Pilot a sport drone on a course or race
entries.localizedDescription: Pilot a sport drone through an obstacle course or race using a visual feed or FPV.

entries.localizedLabel: Pilot a helicopter in a sport event
entries.localizedDescription: Pilot a helicopter in a sport task, flying a route or performing maneuvers under Rotorcraft rules.
Ride slowly through obstacle sections on a motorcycle, maintaining balance and avoiding touches or penalties.

entries.localizedLabel: Take part in a motorcycle rally raid or cross-country event
entries.localizedDescription: Ride a long off-road route in a motorcycle cross-country or rally raid event, following its navigation rules.
Play bandy on an ice field, using sticks to move a ball and score goals under bandy rules.
Play rink bandy, a version of bandy on a smaller ice surface with a corresponding team size and rules.
Play short bandy on a shorter field under the rules of this short-format version.
Play without a racket, using the hand to send the pelota alternately to the front wall of a fronton or trinquet. Protective joint pads do not change the way the game is played.
Play by hand on a court with one front wall, striking a rubber ball into the permitted wall area and returning it to the opponent.
Play frontenis by hitting a ball with a racket against the front wall of a fronton and returning it to the playing area under this form of pelota’s rules. Specialized balls and rackets are used.
Catch the ball in a long, curved cesta, guide or accelerate it along the basket, and throw it at the front wall of the fronton.
Play with a xare ring-shaped racket strung with netting: catch or briefly hold the ball and fling it with a forearm movement rather than striking it with taut strings.
Hit a leather pelota with a short wooden paleta toward the front wall of a fronton or trinquet.
Hit a leather pelota with a heavier, solid short wooden pala on a 36-meter fronton.
Hit a rubber pelota with a wooden, carbon-fiber, or fiberglass paleta on a fronton or in a trinquet.
Wrestle in a dohyō, trying to push an opponent out of the ring or make any part of their body other than the soles of their feet touch its inner surface.
Pull a rope as a team in a sport competition, trying to move the opposing team beyond a designated line.
Slide and steer a special Icestock stick over a playing surface toward a target area or in relation to other sticks. The game is played on ice in winter and on an approved hard surface in summer.
Take part in pool lifesaving by completing swimming stages, moving a mannequin, and using rescue equipment according to the discipline’s format.

entries.localizedLabel: Compete in beach or ocean lifesaving
entries.localizedDescription: Take part in beach or ocean lifesaving events, completing running, swimming, or rescue-craft stages.

entries.localizedLabel: Compete in a team SERC rescue simulation
entries.localizedDescription: As a team, assess a set emergency scenario and complete a sequence of rescue and first-aid actions within a time limit in a SERC competition. This is a controlled team competition, not a real-world rescue. Recording the whole event is valid; the simulated response actions need not be split out.

entries.localizedLabel: Race in a surf boat or IRB lifesaving event
entries.localizedDescription: Take part in lifesaving races in watercraft, including rowing rescue boats and inflatable motorized rescue boats.
Play contract bridge with a partner: bid a contract and then work together to play the card tricks.

entries.localizedLabel: Race a powerboat on a circuit
entries.localizedDescription: Race a high-speed motorboat around a circuit, steering the boat and competing for speed.

entries.localizedLabel: Compete in an offshore powerboat race
entries.localizedDescription: Race a motorboat over an open-water course, competing for speed or placement.
Pilot a radio-controlled motor racing boat around a marked water course.
Race a motorized personal watercraft on the water.
Ride a motor-powered MotoSurf board, performing maneuvers or runs on the water.
Perform figures, balance elements, gymnastic and choreographic sequences on an artistic cycling bike, individually, in pairs, or in a group according to the chosen format.
Perform gymnastics exercises and routines on one or more apparatus.
Perform artistic and dance routines on roller skates, individually, in pairs, or in a group. The program type and composition depend on the chosen discipline.
Play hockey with a ball on a sand court under Beach Hockey rules.
Wrestle standing inside a small circle on sand, trying to score with a throw or control, or force the opponent out of the circle.
Grip an opponent’s belt or clothing and use throws or holds under the rules of the selected official belt-wrestling style.

entries.localizedLabel: Shoot at a biathlon rifle range
